hypothesis: Giving dense retrieval sequences equal total objective weight may improve temporal transfer and reduce task interference; this is not an established root cause.
selection_entities: new generated pool, disjoint from training
selection_wording: unseen development frames; previously inspected template family
primary_endpoint: fixed final checkpoint exact answer prefix on fresh selection items
secondary_endpoint: fixed final checkpoint summed option likelihood on the existing 500 QA dev items

full_run_gate.interpretation: Practical exploratory gate, not a confirmatory statistical test. If not met, retain R7 and do not launch a full run for this hypothesis.

controls: Same initial tensors, serialized training examples, data permutation, selection examples, optimizer, learning rate 1e-4, warmup 30, batch 32, workers 4. Only dense retrieval normalization differs.
caveats: Sequence normalization also increases the relative objective weight of copy replay; it does not isolate temporal weighting alone.
One seed and short continuation; a failed pilot does not rule out all weighted curricula.
The 500-item dev set has been reused; improvements remain exploratory development evidence.
No locked test data or answers are used.
